newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mobil operations unaffected by ship fire.
newsitem.headline: Mobil operations unaffected by ship fire.

text.p: Operations at the 300,000-barrel per day (bpd) Mobil Oil Singapore refinery were not affected by a fire aboard a product tanker berthed at the refinery's terminal, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
The 26,909-dwt Ocean Trader was berthed at Jurong Terminal when the fire broke out at 1020 GMT on Wednesday.
Two crew members were injured and another two were reported missing, the Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) said in a statement.
The Mobil spokeswoman said Ocean Trader had remained at the berth overnight while investigations were carried out into the cause of the fire.
She said she did not immediately know when the ship would be allowed to leave the berth.
However, she said that the fire on the ship, which was discharging condensate -- a very light crude oil -- at the time of the fire, had not affected the refinery's operations.
A Mobil statement earlier said the Ocean Trader is a Singapore registered ship owned by Ocean Tanker.
The refinery is in the process of returning from a major maintenance period. The whole refinery was closed down on March 15 for more than five weeks.
On Tuesday, Mobil said it had restarted the refinery and expected oil product output to be on-specification by the end of this week.
The refinery's capacity was boosted during the maintenance to 300,000 bpd from 280,000 bpd.
